citations.title: Licensing Procedures
citations.requirement: The applicant must be 21 or older and disclose owners of 25% or more, prior license actions, and criminal charges and Medicare/Medicaid violations. The application needs a business plan (1-year budget, populations served, services), the .08B policies, proof of workers' compensation, and a $1,000 nonrefundable fee for a 3-year license. A license is valid 3 years. Renewal needs a $1,000 fee, substantively changed policies (complaints, client evaluation), valid licenses and certificates for current employees, and an annual data collection survey. OHCQ may inspect before deciding, may approve with conditions (management firm up to 24 months, or a term under 1 year), and may issue provisional licenses. It may charge $250 per additional pre-licensure visit.

citations.title: Administration
citations.requirement: The agency must have a governing authority that meets at least annually with management to review and advise on policies and keeps minutes (participants, agenda, actions). It must develop and implement policies on: scope of services, care coordination, admission criteria, pre-acceptance assessment, billing and service records, QA, and clinical management (assessment, plans, delegation, supervision). It also needs policies on job descriptions and qualifications, skill assessments, and employee health requirements. Patient care policies cover skilled-service criteria, administration of drugs, frequency of client monitoring, and training of clients and families. Informed consent policies cover plan-of-care changes and routine treatments or medication self-administration by non-licensed staff. Environment and safety policies cover infection control, biomedical waste, equipment, and emergency procedures. OHCQ may waive a policy if the agency gives a written explanation.

citations.title: Complaint Process
citations.requirement: The agency needs an internal complaint process with client notice, investigation protocols, and timely handling of written complaints without disrupting services. Each investigation report states time, date, place and people involved, a full description, the disposition, and follow-up to prevent recurrence. If no investigation is done, the reason must be documented. The agency notifies the client or representative, the physician if needed, and licensing or law enforcement agencies when required. Clients must be given OHCQ's complaint hotline number. Investigation reports go to OHCQ immediately on request, and a public summary is available on request as permitted by law.

citations.title: Employee, Independent Contractor, and Contractual Employee Requirements
citations.requirement: Pre-referral screening must include: criminal history check (State or private) under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19; licensure or certification verification; basic health screening including TB; references; employment history; I-9; identity and employment eligibility; an in-person interview; and a skills assessment and demonstration. Training records go in the personnel file, and screening records are kept in the agency's business office. A non-certified caregiver may be provided only if the client needs no ADL help, only needs ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or signs a waiver of skilled services. A certified caregiver is required for clients who need one for ADLs or for medication administration. Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action must be reported immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ. Subcontract agencies must verify personnel information and give evidence of that to the contracting agency.

citations.title: Training
citations.requirement: Referred individuals must be appropriately trained. Outside trainers need OHCQ's written approval. Minimum content for in-home care: instruction and supervised practice in personal care; recognizing situations that need RN referral, including significant change in condition; record keeping; ethics and confidentiality; CPR; standard precautions; and prevention of abuse and neglect.

citations.title: Services Provided
citations.requirement: An RN assesses each new client who requires skilled services and ADL help, helps develop the plan of care and assign staff, decides whether a CNA is needed, and helps train staff. Assessment is required: when services are requested; before services start (with limited exceptions); within 48 hours for listed skilled needs or a significant change of condition (7 calendar days if the RN documents the 48-hour assessment is unnecessary); on client request; and at least annually. The care plan must state services, when and how often, who provides them and how, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures. Informed consent and waivers need a documented risk/benefit discussion, a signed and dated form, and a copy in the record. RN on-site supervision is required at least every 45 days if staff administer medications, every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration, and every 4 months otherwise, or more often as the RN decides. Supervision must be documented. Medication administration requires licensed or certified staff, physician orders, and documentation of medications, errors and adverse reactions. On-call: 24/7 contact, response within 1 hour, a call log, and written on-call procedures given to clients.

citations.title: Client Representative
citations.requirement: The agency must recognize a guardian of the person or property, an advance directive, a surrogate decision maker, a power of attorney, a representative payee, or a person designated in writing by a competent client. It may not honor a representative who exceeds the authority granted. It must document the representative's name or keep the authorizing document in the record.

citations.title: Maintenance of Records
citations.requirement: Client records are kept 5 years after discharge. For minors, keep until age 21 or 5 years after the record is made, whichever is later. If the agency closes, records must be returned to the client or representative or retained as required. Records are confidential and released only with written consent or as permitted by Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3. Discharged client records must be completed within 30 days of discharge. Safeguards must protect against loss, destruction and unauthorized use.

citations.title: Client's Rights and Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Written rights policies must be available to clients. Clients must receive: a cost estimate; a statement of costs not covered by third parties; itemized bills on request; the caregiver's name; the name and contact of the care supervisor; the 24/7 phone number; and disclosure of subcontractual relationships. Rights include dignity, participation in the care plan, refusing treatment, privacy, freedom from abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation, confidentiality, and complaints without retaliation with a prompt response. Clients must have access to complaint procedures for OHCQ and for Adult or Child Protective Services. The agency must give advance directive information and obtain the client's advance directive information. It must honor refusal of treatment and waivers of skilled services. Informed consent information must cover purpose, alternatives, side effects and benefits, cost, and the right to withdraw. Clients may accept or reject any referred caregiver without retaliation.

citations.title: Conditions for Provider Participation — General Requirements
citations.requirement: The provider must meet the COMAR 10.09.36 Medicaid conditions and obtain written verification of worker qualifications. Incidents and complaints are reported within 24 hours of knowledge, with a written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form. The local department of social services is notified immediately of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation (COMAR 07.02.16). The provider must cooperate with inspections, reviews and audits. It bills only services preauthorized in the plan of service, delivered consistent with it, and within the provider agreement. Service documentation (dates and hours) is kept 6 years from date of service. Services may not be suspended, terminated, increased or reduced without Department authorization and consultation with the participant, and a transition plan goes to the case manager or supports planner and participant. Medicaid eligibility is verified at the start of each month of service. The provider may not have unpaid overpayments and must be free of conflicts of interest. Providers and principals must be free of 24-month look-back events: license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citations affecting health and safety, and agreement terminations.

citations.title: Specific Conditions for Provider Participation — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: The provider must hold an RSA license (the text says to provide 'Level Two or Level Three home care services') and employ an RN. The RN assesses each new participant, helps develop worker instructions and assign staff, delegates nursing tasks to a CNA or CMT under COMAR 10.27.11, and instructs workers. Workers must accept instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or NP, or MDH. Participants must have a significant role in directing services, including selecting, training, scheduling, setting duties for and dismissing their worker. The provider gives MDH 45 days' written notice of closure, change of ownership, location, name or tax ID, or sale, including how participants will be informed and a transition plan. It must apply for a new license on a transfer of ownership. It collects the participant's (or representative's) signature at least monthly verifying services. Criminal history checks are required for all direct service workers, including nurses. Workers who administer medications must be CMTs, and workers who perform other delegated nursing functions must also be CNAs. The participant's representative may not be assigned as the worker.

citations.title: Payment Procedures
citations.requirement: To be paid for personal assistance, the provider and its workers must use the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system to document time and submit claims. Billing time limits come from COMAR 10.09.36.06. The provider is paid the lesser of its usual and customary charge to the general public or the fee schedule rate. Services up to 12 hours/day are paid in 15-minute units, and a daily rate applies above 12 hours. The Department publishes the fee schedule at least annually. Rates rise 3% each July 1, subject to the State budget.

citations.title: Covered Services — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: Defines the covered personal assistance services (ADL/IADL help per the plan of service). Section text was not re-fetched in this pass; it comes from the supplied fact-checked research (S36).

citations.title: Limitations
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S57): services are limited to a service budget based on assessed need. Escort and travel expenses are not covered, and housekeeping unrelated to ADLs is not covered.

citations.title: Participant Eligibility
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S35): institutional level of care, Medicaid eligibility, and living at home are required. The plan of service names the personal assistance agency the participant chooses.

citations.title: Nurse Monitoring providers
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S37): nurse monitoring providers are designated by the Department under §1915(b)(4). The agency coordinates with the participant's nurse monitor.

citations.title: Covered Services — Nurse Monitoring
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S56): nurse monitoring contact every 6 months and an in-person visit every 12 months. Agency staff must cooperate with the nurse monitor.

citations.title: CPAS — Specific Conditions for Provider Participation — Personal Assistance
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S49): CPAS personal assistance providers must hold an RSA license, employ an RN, and meet the parallel participation conditions that apply to CFC.

citations.title: Billing Time Limitations
citations.requirement: Referenced in COMAR 10.09.84.24C as the source of Medicaid billing time limits. The 12-month claim limit comes from the CFC Billing Manual (C37). The section text was not fetched.

citations.title: Cause for Suspension or Removal and Imposition of Sanctions
citations.requirement: Referenced in COMAR 10.09.84.05B(3) and in PT 13-27 as the basis for Medicaid suspension, removal and sanctions. The section text was not fetched.

citations.title: RSA worker-classification certification for personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the OHCQ RSA page (research S1): the person who controls pay and employment practices must read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submit the online RSA Certification form. This is a condition of obtaining and keeping the license.

citations.title: Criminal history records checks for direct service workers
citations.requirement: Cited in COMAR 10.07.05.10B(1)(a) and 10.09.84.06A(11) as the procedure for State criminal history records checks (or private agency background checks) on direct service workers, including nurses.

citations.title: Adult Protective Services
citations.requirement: Cited in COMAR 10.09.84.05A(3)(c) as the basis for immediately notifying the local department of social services when there is reason to believe a participant has been subjected to abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation. Only the cross-reference was verified. The chapter text was not fetched.

citations.title: Residential Service Agencies Provider Compliance Audits (Aug. 10, 2026)
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S38): DPICC audits RSAs, and non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts. Respond to a plan of correction within 15 calendar days. Repeat findings within 6 months can bring sanctions under COMAR 10.09.36.

citations.title: Updates for the Home and Community-Based Services Cost Survey
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S12): the annual HCBS Cost Survey is due Dec. 31, 2026. Payment is suspended from Jan. 1, 2027 for non-filers.

citations.title: MPRIME Launch — Day One Provider Actions and Enrollment Policy Updates
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S39): MPRIME went live Oct. 13, 2026. A complete application by Dec. 31, 2026 can be backdated. An SDAT ID in good standing is required, and MPRIME auto-suspends providers that lose it. License uploads are due by March 31, 2027, and expired licenses trigger suspension from April 1, 2027.

citations.title: FY 2025 Rates for CFC and CPAS (effective July 1, 2024)
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S9, S14, S15): W5519 (CFC) and W5527 (CPAS) are $6.3962 per 15-minute unit. Shared attendant is $4.2597 per 15 minutes (W5521/W5528). The daily rate for more than 12 hours per day is $329.84 (W5532). Rates were reported unchanged as of July 1, 2025 and level in the FY 2027 budget.

citations.title: Federal EVV requirement for Medicaid personal care services
citations.requirement: Federal requirement for electronic visit verification of Medicaid personal care services. Maryland meets it through the state telephonic system (ISAS).

citations.title: Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule — payment adequacy and rate transparency
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S43): an 80% direct-care compensation standard, applicable from July 9, 2030 per MDH's 2024 report, plus rate transparency. RSAs must also file an annual personal care aide wage report with the Department of Labor by Sept. 1 (HB 189/SB 371 of 2024).

citations.cite: Maryland Minimum Wage and Overtime Law (MDOL guidance)
citations.title: Maryland Minimum Wage and Overtime Law
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S21): the State minimum is $15.00 and overtime is due after 40 hours. Howard County is $16.00. Montgomery County from July 1, 2026 is $16.50 for home care employers with 11+ employees that get at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid, and otherwise $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50) or $15.95 (10 or fewer). No statute section number is cited because none was verified.

citations.cite: Maryland Healthy Working Families Act (MDOL FAQs)
citations.title: Earned Sick and Safe Leave
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S27): 1 hour accrues per 30 hours worked, with a 40-hour annual accrual. Leave is paid for employers with 15+ employees. Statutory caps beyond that should be confirmed with MDOL before the policy is finalized.

citations.cite: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission — Questions and Answers for Employers
citations.title: Workers' compensation coverage
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S26): every employer with one or more employees must provide workers' compensation coverage. Proof is also required for the RSA application under COMAR 10.07.05.04A(2)(j).

citations.title: Changes in an Agency That Affect the Operating License
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents. Its text was not fetched. The OHCQ RSA page (S1) requires 45 days' written notice of a change of ownership and has separate forms for added services, address, name and branch changes.

citations.title: Public Representation
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs how the agency represents itself publicly. Its text was not fetched. Read it before finalizing advertising wording.

citations.title: Inspection by the Department
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs OHCQ inspections. Its text was not fetched.

citations.title: Clinical Records
citations.requirement: The section exists per the chapter table of contents and governs clinical record content. Its text could not be fetched. Confirm required record elements before finalizing the record-content checklist.

citations.title: Community First Choice Billing Manual
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S10): personal assistance is documented and paid through ISAS, which generates claims. Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service.

citations.title: ISAS provider training
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S46): participant primary landline or OTP device verification, up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles, a missing-time limit of 4 requests due within 2 business days after month-end, a Thursday–Wednesday workweek, and help desk 1-855-463-5877. These details are from 2020 training, so confirm them with the ISAS Help Desk.

citations.cite: OLTSS SOP — Standardized Times for Assistance with ADLs, IADLs and Delegated Nursing Tasks (rev. April 29, 2025)
citations.title: Standardized task times
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S51): OLTSS standard times used when planning and authorizing assistance with ADLs, IADLs and delegated nursing tasks.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S4): defines residential service agency, home health care, certified care and ADLs/IADLs. A residential service agency employs or contracts workers to provide at least one home health care service to an unrelated sick or disabled person at home.

citations.title: Replacement of Personal Emergency Response Systems
citations.requirement: Per the supplied research (S50): lists Maryland Access Point (1-844-MAP-LINK) and OLTSS (410-767-1739) as contacts for PERS and community resources.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Authority and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Maryland term is 'governing authority'. It must convene at least annually with management staff to review and advise on policies.
Minutes must record the participants, agenda items considered, and actions taken.

COMAR 10.07.05 sets no administrator credential or client-to-staff ratio. The policy should still define job descriptions and qualifications for the director, the RN, and the scheduler/billing coordinator.
The agency must employ an RN if it serves CFC/CPAS participants.
Keep the organizational chart that was submitted with the license application current.

policies.title: Licensure, License Renewal and Public Representation
state_specifics: The RSA license is valid for 3 years from issuance. Renewal requires a $1,000 nonrefundable fee under COMAR; OHCQ's 06/26/2026 application says there is no fee to apply, so confirm when the fee is billed.

The renewal packet includes changed policies (complaint handling, client evaluation and assessment), valid professional licenses and certificates for all current employees, and the annual data collection survey.
Keep the original license application attachments on file (business plan, organizational chart, workers' compensation proof).
COMAR 10.07.05.06 (Public Representation) governs advertising. Its text was not retrieved, so read it before approving any marketing wording.
OHCQ RSA Team: 410-402-8040. OHCQ complaint line: 800-492-6005.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The governing authority reviews policies at least annually, and the minutes record the review.
Maintain a version log. At renewal, submit any policy that changed substantively, especially complaint handling and client evaluation/assessment.
If a COMAR 10.07.05.08B policy is not applicable, request OHCQ's written waiver and keep the written explanation on file.
The COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1) topics in the manual map to the .08B list.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: A quality assurance program is a required administration policy.
Inputs should include complaint investigation reports, incident reports (24-hour and 7-day), RN supervisory-visit documentation, missed-visit and ISAS exception data, and audit findings.
Review results at the annual governing authority meeting and record actions in the minutes.
Track compliance with the 45-day, 3-month and 4-month RN supervisory-visit intervals and the 1-hour on-call response.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only services that were preauthorized in the plan of service, delivered consistent with it, and within the provider agreement.
A provider with unpaid overpayments, or a principal of one, may not participate.

The provider and its principals must be free of the 24-month look-back events: license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citations affecting health and safety, and agreement termination.
Providers must be free of conflicts of interest, and the agency must cooperate with inspections, reviews and audits.
The provider is paid the lesser of its usual and customary charge or the fee schedule rate, so private-pay rates should not be set below the Medicaid rate.
Monitor the share of Medicaid payments spent on direct-care compensation against the federal 80% standard (compliance date July 9, 2030 per MDH).
Include a non-retaliation reporting channel, exclusion-list screening of staff, and a billing-error correction and refund procedure.

policies.title: Change of Ownership, Location, Name, Tax ID or Closure (45-Day Notice)
state_specifics: Give MDH at least 45 days' written notice before voluntary closure, change of ownership, change of location, sale, name change, or provider tax ID change.
The notice must state how participants and representatives will be told and must include the transition plan to keep services continuous.
A new owner must apply for a new RSA license and, to keep serving Medicaid participants, submit a Medicaid provider application.
OHCQ also expects 45 days' notice of a change of ownership. Use the OHCQ forms for added services, address, name and branch changes.
On closure, return records to clients or their representatives or keep them for the required period.

policies.title: Medicaid Provider Enrollment (PT 76), MPRIME, SDAT Good Standing and HCBS Cost Survey
state_specifics: Enrollment is through MPRIME as provider type 76, which launched Oct. 13, 2026. Provider Services: 1-844-463-7768.
A complete application filed by Dec. 31, 2026 can be backdated. Applications without an SDAT ID in good standing are rejected, and MPRIME auto-suspends providers that fall out of good standing.
Upload the RSA license by March 31, 2027 and after every renewal. Expired licenses cause suspension from April 1, 2027.
File the annual HCBS Cost Survey. The FY 2026 survey is due Dec. 31, 2026, and non-filers are suspended from Jan. 1, 2027 until filed.
Verify each participant's Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service.
Assign an owner for the SDAT annual report and personal property return (due April 15).

policies.title: RSA Compliance Audits, Plans of Correction and Sanctions
state_specifics: DPICC runs RSA provider compliance audits. Questions go to mdh.cfcprovidersrsas@maryland.gov.
Respond to every audit outreach. Non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts.
Submit a plan of correction within 15 calendar days. Repeat findings within 6 months can bring sanctions under COMAR 10.09.36.
Designate one responsible person and keep a log of audit requests, due dates and submissions.
Keep the 6-year service documentation (dates, hours, monthly signatures, ISAS records) retrievable on request.

policies.title: Subcontracted Agencies and Contract Caregivers
state_specifics: Screening duties apply equally to independent contractors and contractual employees.

If the agency subcontracts with another licensed agency, that agency must verify the personnel information required by COMAR 10.07.05.10B and give the contracting agency evidence the verification was done.
Clients must be told in writing about any subcontractual relationship with an individual or agency who will be assigned to them.
Note that CFC/CPAS require the agency itself to employ the RN. The aide classification must align with the Health-General §19-4A-11 certification.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Provide the written rights and responsibilities policy to every client or representative.

Rights to list: dignity and individuality; adequate and appropriate care; participating in care planning; refusing treatment after consequences are explained; privacy; freedom from mental, verbal, sexual and physical abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation; confidentiality.
Clients may complain to the agency, government agencies or others without threat or fear of retaliation, and must get a prompt response.
Give clients the procedure for complaining to OHCQ (800-492-6005) and to Adult Protective Services at the local department of social services (Child Protective Services if the client is a minor).
Provide the client's 24/7 agency number, the caregiver's name, and the supervisor's name and contact information.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Notify clients of the internal complaint process and the OHCQ hotline (800-492-6005).
Written complaints must be investigated timely, and services may not be disrupted because a complaint was filed.
Each investigation report records time, date, place and individuals involved, a complete description, the disposition, and follow-up steps to prevent recurrence.
If no investigation is done, document the reason in the complaint record.
Notify the client or representative, the physician if needed, and licensing or law enforcement agencies when required.
Make reports available to OHCQ immediately on request, and a public summary on request as permitted by law.
For Medicaid participants, report complaints within 24 hours of knowledge, with a written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Release medical information only with written consent of the client or representative, or as permitted by Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3.
Records must have safeguards against loss, destruction and illegal or unauthorized use.
Training must include ethical behavior and confidentiality.
Document the client representative with authority to receive information (COMAR 10.07.05.13).
Include breach assessment, notification, minimum-necessary and device security procedures.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Exploitation is a prohibited act under client rights and a mandatory report to the local department of social services.
Medicaid providers must be free of conflicts of interest.
Training on abuse and neglect prevention should cover exploitation.
Policy points: no borrowing, gifts or wills or power-of-attorney involvement; no handling client funds beyond documented errands; receipts for purchases made for clients.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
state_specifics: Clients are entitled to dignity and individuality, and may accept or reject any referred caregiver without retaliation.
No COMAR 10.07.05 section sets language access rules. Use Title VI and ADA obligations.
Provide interpreter or translation access and effective communication for clients with disabilities.
Give clients written rights and complaint information in an understandable form.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Cost Estimates, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Before services start, give a written estimate of costs for the requested services.
Give a statement of what the client pays if services are not covered by third-party payors.
Itemized billing with dates of service and unit charge must be available on request.
Disclose any subcontractual relationship for assigned caregivers.
For Medicaid, payment is the lesser of usual and customary charge or the fee schedule rate. Personal assistance is paid in 15-minute units up to 12 hours per day and by daily rate above.
Current CFC/CPAS rate is $6.3962 per 15 minutes (W5519/W5527); shared attendant $4.2597 per 15 minutes (W5521/W5528). Confirm the current fee schedule before use.

policies.title: Informed Consent and Waiver of Skilled Services
state_specifics: Only a cognitively capable adult client (not a representative) may waive certified care for routine treatments or medication self-administration, or waive recommended skilled care.
Consent follows a documented discussion of risks and benefits. The form is signed and dated by the client or representative with legal authority and kept in the record.
A waiver of skilled services form must be signed by the cognitively capable adult client and kept in the record.
Consent information covers the purpose and nature of treatment, alternatives, side effects and benefits, estimated costs and the right to withdraw.
A non-certified caregiver may be provided only in the three situations in COMAR 10.07.05.10D.

policies.title: Client Representatives and Advance Directives
state_specifics: Recognize guardians of the person or property, advance directives, surrogate decision makers, powers of attorney, representative payees, and persons designated by a competent client in writing.
Do not recognize a representative who exceeds the authority granted by the instrument or by State law.
Document the representative's name or keep the authorizing document in the record.
Give every client information on advance directives and the right to have one, and obtain information about the client's advance directive to assess its effect on care.
A Medicaid participant's representative may not be assigned to work as that participant's caregiver.

policies.title: Client Choice, Participant Direction and Right to Accept or Reject Caregivers
state_specifics: Participants direct the services in their plan of service and may select, train, schedule, set duties for, and dismiss the personal assistance worker in their home.
Workers must accept instruction on required services from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or NP, or MDH.
Participants choose their agency during plan-of-service development, and the plan names the agency.
Clients of any payer may accept or reject any referred caregiver without fear of retaliation.
Reassignment of a rejected caregiver must not interrupt authorized services.

policies.title: Scope of Services — What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: The scope of services is a required .08B policy and must match the services checked on the OHCQ application.

Medicaid personal assistance covers ADL/IADL tasks in the plan of service. Escort and travel expenses are not covered, and housekeeping unrelated to ADLs is not covered. Services are limited to the service budget based on assessed need.
The agency must say whether it accepts clients with skilled needs (wound or catheter care, ventilator care, infusion and so on). If it does, an RN assessment within 48 hours is required.
Nursing tasks may be done only by staff licensed or certified for them. Under CFC, delegated nursing tasks require a CNA, and medication administration requires a CMT.
Use the OLTSS standardized times SOP for task time planning.

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Admission criteria and assessment of potential clients before acceptance are required .08B policies.
CFC participants need institutional level of care, Medicaid eligibility and a home residence, and the plan of service must name the agency.
Verify Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service.
Assessment is required before services begin, with limited exceptions: no request for skilled care and no reason to believe skilled care is needed.
Document the client representative and advance directive information at intake.
Provide the client rights packet, cost estimate, caregiver name, supervisor contact, 24/7 number and on-call procedures.

policies.title: RN Assessment, Plan of Care / Plan of Service and Plan Updates
state_specifics: An RN assesses each new client who needs skilled services and ADL help, and each new CFC/CPAS participant who needs personal assistance.

The plan of care must be based on assessments of health, function and psychosocial condition. It must state services, when and how often, how and by whom, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures.

Reassess: at least annually, on client or representative request, and within 48 hours for listed skilled needs or a significant change in condition. The 48-hour deadline becomes 7 calendar days if the RN documents the reason in the record.
Exceptions for weather emergencies, natural disasters and declared emergencies apply to the assessment timing in .12C(2).
Match scheduled hours to the Medicaid plan of service and do not exceed authorized hours.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight, Delegation and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: The RN provides oversight of care-plan implementation, delegation, supervision and training.

On-site supervision is required at least every 45 days if staff administer medications, every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration, and every 4 months if neither. The RN may set a shorter interval based on the client's condition.
Document each supervisory visit accurately.
CFC/CPAS require the agency to employ an RN who delegates nursing tasks to CNAs or CMTs under COMAR 10.27.11 and instructs workers.
Coordinate with the participant's nurse monitor, who has contact every 6 months and an in-person visit every 12 months.

policies.title: Assigning Certified Caregivers (CNA/CMT) and Non-Certified Aides
state_specifics: A certified caregiver is required for clients who need a certified caregiver for ADLs or who need medication administered.

A non-certified caregiver may be provided only if the client needs no ADL help, needs ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or signs a waiver of skilled services.
The RN determines whether the client needs a CNA or whether a non-certified individual may serve.
CFC: a worker who administers medication under the plan of service must be a CMT. A worker performing other delegated nursing functions must also be a CNA.
Document the RN's determination in the client record.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Administration of drugs is a required .08B policy.

Where staff administer medications, they must be licensed or certified (CMTs under CFC), medications are given only as ordered by the physician, and the client record must document medications administered or taken, medication errors, and adverse drug reactions with corrective action.

A client who signs informed consent may receive assistance from a non-licensed individual with self-administration. This raises RN supervisory visit frequency to every 3 months, and every 45 days where staff administer.
Aides must not administer, adjust or set up medications beyond the plan of care and delegation.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Do not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services for a Medicaid participant without Department authorization and consultation with the participant.
Schedule within authorized plan-of-service hours. When two participants share an aide, use the shared-attendant codes.
Participants may direct the schedule and dismiss a worker, so make a backup caregiver available.
Notify the RN and the supports planner of repeated missed visits.
Maintain the 24/7 on-call line so clients can report a missed visit at any time.
The participant's representative may not be assigned as the worker.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification (ISAS) and Timekeeping
state_specifics: The provider and its workers must use the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system to document time and submit claims for personal assistance.

Aides call to clock in and out at the start and end of each shift. Visits are verified from the participant's primary landline or an OTP device, and an aide's phone number must never match the client's.
Aides cannot log into the ISAS portal. The agency may have up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles.

2020 ISAS training described a limit of 4 missing-time requests, each with a reason, due within 2 business days after month-end, with hours above the plan of service reduced automatically. Confirm the current rules with the ISAS Help Desk (1-855-463-5877).
The CFC Billing Manual requires claims within 12 months of the date of service.

policies.title: Monthly Participant Signature, Eligibility Verification and Service Documentation
state_specifics: At least monthly, collect and keep the participant's (or representative's) signature verifying services rendered.
Verify Medicaid eligibility at the beginning of each month of service.
Keep documentation of dates and hours of services for 6 years from date of service in a manner approved by the Department.
Reconcile ISAS time to the monthly signature log and the plan of service before billing.
Obtain written verification of the qualifications of all workers and provide a copy of the license or credentials on request.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Training must teach aides to identify situations that need RN referral, including significant changes in a client's condition.
A significant change requires RN assessment within 48 hours, or within 7 calendar days if the RN documents that 48 hours is not needed.
Give aides the on-call number and require a call for emergency inquiries. Staff respond consistent with medical and nursing standards.
Report incidents within 24 hours of knowledge and file the written report within 7 calendar days.
Aides call 911 for life-threatening emergencies, then the agency.

policies.title: 24/7 On-Call Services
state_specifics: Clients or representatives must be able to contact an agency representative by communication device 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Emergency inquiries must be recognized and routed to an individual who can respond under medical and nursing standards.
Response is required no later than 1 hour after the agency receives the inquiry, or sooner if medical standards require.
Keep a log of inquiries with the identity of response personnel, content of the inquiry and time of each inquiry.
Give clients written procedures and the phone number for on-call service.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer, Suspension and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: For Medicaid participants, do not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services without Department authorization and consultation with the participant or representative.
Submit a transition plan to the case manager or supports planner and the participant when suspending or terminating services.
Complete discharged-client records within 30 days of discharge and keep them 5 years after discharge (6 years from date of service for Medicaid).
Give 45 days' notice to MDH for agency closure, sale or similar events, with the transition plan.
The client may withdraw from treatment at any time, and the agency must explain associated risks.

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs, Supports Planners and Payers
state_specifics: CFC (COMAR 10.09.84) and CPAS (COMAR 10.09.20) both require an RSA license and an employed RN.
Coordinate with the participant's supports planner and nurse monitor, and share documented participant information on the Department's forms and procedures.
Maryland Access Point: 1-844-MAP-LINK. OLTSS: 410-767-1739. CFC/RSA compliance questions: mdh.cfcprovidersrsas@maryland.gov.
For clients on managed-care benefit plans or other third-party payors, maintain records as the payor requires.
Agency policy should state how care coordination within the agency or with other providers is delineated and communicated to the client.

policies.title: Medicaid Billing, Rates, Claims and Overpayment Recovery
state_specifics: Claims are generated through ISAS for personal assistance. Submit within the billing time limit (12 months per the CFC Billing Manual; COMAR 10.09.36.06 sets the regulatory limit).
Payment is the lesser of usual and customary charge or the published fee schedule.
15-minute units apply up to 12 hours per day, with a daily rate above that.
Rates rise 3% each July 1 subject to the State budget, but the FY 2026 and FY 2027 rates were reported level. Verify rates against the current fee schedule.
Providers with outstanding overpayments cannot participate, so refund overpayments promptly.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Training must include prevention of abuse and neglect.
Clients have the right to be free from mental, verbal, sexual and physical abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation.

For Medicaid participants, notify the local department of social services immediately when there is reason to believe a participant has been subjected to abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation (COMAR 07.02.16).
Also report the incident within 24 hours and file the written report within 7 calendar days.
Report conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action to the Board and OHCQ immediately. OHCQ complaint line: 800-492-6005.
Make clients aware of APS access (or CPS for minors).

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Report incidents and complaints within 24 hours of knowledge of the event.
Submit a written report within 7 calendar days on the form designated by the Department.
Notify the local department of social services immediately for suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation.
Record medication errors and adverse drug reactions in the client record with corrective action.
Notify the Board of Nursing and OHCQ immediately of known conduct that may be grounds for Board action.
Aggregate incidents for QA review.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Infection control procedures and disposal of biomedical waste are required .08B policies.
Training must include standard precautions for infection control.
Provide employees with PPE and handwashing supplies and a bloodborne pathogen exposure plan consistent with OSHA where aides have occupational exposure.
TB screening is part of caregiver screening before referral.
No separate COMAR 10.07.05 section on vaccinations was verified.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Emergency procedures are a required policy under COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(e)(v). No separate RSA emergency-preparedness section was found.
The assessment timing exceptions for weather-related emergencies, natural disasters, and federal, state or local emergency declarations apply to assessments only, not to service duties.
The plan should rank clients by risk, name an emergency contact for each, and establish a call tree.
Keep the 24/7 on-call line operating in emergencies.
Maryland Access Point (1-844-MAP-LINK) can help with community resources.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: No COMAR 10.07.05 section addresses caregiver safety beyond the environment and safety policy requirement.
Workers' compensation is mandatory for any employer with one or more employees, and injuries must be reported.
The care plan must include safety measures to protect against injury.
Policy points: home safety assessment at intake, right to leave an unsafe home, violence and harassment reporting, and no retaliation.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Medicaid does not pay for escort or travel expenses under CFC, so the agency should not bill for client transport time.
State clearly whether aides may drive clients. If permitted, require a valid license, insurance, and a client consent form.
Non-owned auto liability coverage is recommended. COMAR sets no liability insurance minimum.
Mileage reimbursement is a wage-hour issue under PER-06.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Certification (CNA/CMT) and License Verification
state_specifics: Verify current professional licensure or certification before referral.
Obtain written verification of the qualifications of all individuals who render services.
Certified aides are required when a client needs ADL help from a certified caregiver or medication administration.
Under CFC, medication administration requires a CMT, and other delegated nursing functions require a CNA as well.
Report conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action immediately to the Board and OHCQ.

policies.title: Criminal History Records Checks and Pre-Referral Screening
state_specifics: Complete a State criminal history records check (or private agency background check) before referral, under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19.
CFC requires checks on all direct service workers, including nurses.

The screening set also includes references, employment history, I-9, identity and employment eligibility, a basic health screening with TB, an in-person interview, and a skills assessment before client referral.
Add exclusion-list screening (OIG and Maryland Medicaid) as a company policy for Medicaid participation.
Keep the records in the business office.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: Minimum content: supervised personal care practice, RN referral triggers, record keeping, ethics and confidentiality, CPR, standard precautions, and abuse and neglect prevention.
A skills assessment and demonstration are required before client referral.
Outside trainers need OHCQ written approval before they train.
Keep training records in each personnel file.
COMAR 10.07.05.11 sets no annual hours. State any annual refresher requirement as agency policy, and the RN trains and retrains staff when indicated.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: A basic health screening, including TB screening, is required before the individual is referred to clients.
Employee health requirements are a required .08B policy.
Set re-screening frequency by agency policy because the COMAR text read here gives none.
Keep results in the personnel file kept in the business office.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Records of all screening elements must be kept for each employee, contractor and contractual employee in the agency's business office.
Training records go in the personnel file.
Medicaid documentation of service is retained 6 years from date of service.
Keep copies of current licenses and credentials ready to produce on request.
Keep workers' compensation proof.

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Leave Compliance
state_specifics: State minimum wage is $15.00. Howard County is $16.00. Montgomery County rates from July 1, 2026 are $16.50 for home care employers with 11+ employees that receive at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid, and otherwise $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50) or $15.95 (10 or fewer). Re-check every July 1.
Overtime is due after 40 hours in a workweek. Home care third-party employers are covered by 29 CFR 552, so confirm the current federal status of the companionship exemption.
Earned sick and safe leave: 1 hour per 30 hours worked, 40-hour annual accrual, paid for employers with 15 or more employees.
Workers' compensation is mandatory with one or more employees. FAMLI contributions begin Jan. 1, 2027 at a 0.9% total rate.
Pay travel time between clients where required.
File the annual RSA personal care aide wage report with the Department of Labor by Sept. 1.
Classify aides as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Training includes ethical behavior and confidentiality.
Medicaid providers must be free of conflicts of interest.
A participant's representative may not be assigned as that participant's caregiver.
Workers accept instruction on the plan of service from the participant, nurse monitor, treating clinician or MDH.
Include rules on gifts, social media, personal relationships, and dual relationships.

policies.title: Worker Classification Certification (Health-General §19-4A-11) and Annual PCA Wage Report
state_specifics: The person who controls pay and employment practices must read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submit the online RSA Certification form. It is required both to get and to keep the license.
Aides are classified as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise.
File the annual RSA personal care aide wage report (average, highest and lowest PCA wage rates) with the Department of Labor by Sept. 1 under HB 189/SB 371 of 2024.

policies.title: Job Descriptions, Qualifications and Skill Assessments
state_specifics: COMAR requires job descriptions and educational qualifications for all employees and contractors, and skill assessments of all employees and contractors.
Write descriptions for the director, RN, scheduler/ISAS billing coordinator, and aides (CNA, CMT, non-certified).
The RN position must be an employee when serving CFC/CPAS.
COMAR 10.07.05 sets no administrator credential.

policies.title: Reporting Caregiver Misconduct to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ
state_specifics: If the agency is aware of an action or inaction by a referred individual that may be grounds for action under the Health Occupations Article (including §8-316 and §8-6A-10), it must report to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ immediately.
Nursing administrators, RNs, LPNs and CNAs have immunity under Courts and Judicial Proceedings §5-709 for making the report. Others have immunity under §5-708.
Document the report and the date of submission.

policies.title: Client Records, Clinical Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep client records 5 years after discharge. For minors, keep until age 21 or 5 years after the record is made, whichever is later.
Medicaid service documentation (dates and hours) must be kept 6 years from date of service, so use whichever period is longer.
Complete records of discharged clients within 30 days of discharge.
Records include assessments, plans of care, RN supervisory visit documentation, informed consent and waiver forms, medication documentation, and client representative documentation.
If the agency closes, return records to clients or representatives or retain them as required.
Clinical record content under COMAR 10.07.05.14 was not retrieved. Confirm it before finalizing the record checklist.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Incident and complaint reports: within 24 hours, with a written report within 7 calendar days. Immediate notice to the local department of social services for suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation.
Immediate report to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ for conduct that may be grounds for Board action.
Annual data collection survey with license renewal (every 3 years).
Annual HCBS Cost Survey (FY 2026 due Dec. 31, 2026).
Annual RSA personal care aide wage report to the Department of Labor by Sept. 1.
45-day notices to MDH for closure, sale, ownership, location, name or tax ID changes.
Plans of correction within 15 calendar days of an audit finding.

policies.title: Regulatory Inspections, Surveys and Records Access
state_specifics: Cooperate with required inspections, reviews and audits by authorized government agents.
OHCQ may inspect before approving or denying a license. Each additional pre-licensure visit caused by noncompliance may cost $250.
Make complaint investigation reports available to OHCQ immediately on request.
Designate staff to receive surveyors and keep personnel and client records available in the agency's business office.
COMAR 10.07.05.07 (Inspection by the Department) exists, but its text was not retrieved.

forms.name: Client Rights and Responsibilities Acknowledgment
forms.purpose: Documents delivery of the rights policy, OHCQ hotline (800-492-6005), APS/CPS complaint access, and 24/7 number.

forms.name: Cost Estimate and Private-Pay Responsibility Statement
forms.purpose: Written estimate of costs and the statement of costs the client pays if third-party payors do not cover services.

forms.name: Service Agreement with Subcontract Disclosure
forms.purpose: Records services, rates, caregiver names, supervisor contact, 24/7 phone, and any subcontract relationship.

forms.name: Informed Consent for Changes to Recommended Plan of Care
forms.purpose: Documents the risk/benefit discussion and signed, dated consent.

forms.name: Waiver of Skilled Services
forms.purpose: Signed by a cognitively capable adult client declining recommended certified or skilled care.

forms.name: Client Representative and Advance Directive Information Record
forms.purpose: Documents the representative's authority and advance directive information.

forms.name: RN Initial Assessment
forms.purpose: Health, function and psychosocial assessment before services, and reassessments.

forms.name: Plan of Care / Worker Instructions
forms.purpose: Services, frequency, who provides them, goals and safety measures.

forms.name: RN Supervisory Visit Record
forms.purpose: Documents on-site supervision at the 45-day, 3-month or 4-month interval.

forms.name: Medication Assistance Log and Medication Error/Adverse Reaction Report
forms.purpose: Documents medications administered or taken, errors, adverse reactions and corrective action.

forms.name: On-Call Inquiry Log
forms.purpose: Records identity of response personnel, inquiry content and time for the 1-hour response standard.

forms.name: Monthly Participant Service Verification Signature Sheet
forms.purpose: Participant or representative signature verifying services rendered each month.

forms.name: Monthly Medicaid Eligibility Verification Log
forms.purpose: Documents eligibility verification at the start of each month of service.

forms.name: ISAS Missing-Time/Exception Request Log
forms.purpose: Tracks missing-time requests and reasons before billing.

forms.name: Client Transition Plan
forms.purpose: Continuity plan on suspension, termination, closure or ownership change.

forms.name: Incident and Complaint Report (24-hour notification and 7-day written report)
forms.purpose: Captures the incident and follow-up on the Department's designated form.

forms.name: Suspected Abuse/Neglect/Exploitation Referral Record
forms.purpose: Documents the immediate report to the local department of social services.

forms.name: Complaint Investigation Report
forms.purpose: Time, date, place, individuals, description, disposition and follow-up.

forms.name: Caregiver Screening Checklist
forms.purpose: Documents criminal history check, license verification, TB and health screening, references, employment history, I-9, identity, interview and skills demonstration.

forms.name: Skills Assessment and Competency Checklist
forms.purpose: Documents the pre-referral skills demonstration and training topics.

forms.name: Training Record
forms.purpose: Documents CPR, infection control, abuse prevention and other training, filed in the personnel file.

forms.name: Board of Nursing/OHCQ Misconduct Report Log
forms.purpose: Documents immediate reports of conduct that may be grounds for Board action.

forms.name: Governing Authority Annual Meeting Minutes
forms.purpose: Participants, agenda items and actions taken.

forms.name: 45-Day Notice to MDH
forms.purpose: Notice of closure, ownership, location, name, sale or tax ID change, with participant notification method and transition plan.

forms.name: Audit Response and Plan of Correction Tracker
forms.purpose: Tracks audit outreach, 15-day plan of correction deadlines and sanctions.

forms.name: Annual Regulatory Calendar
forms.purpose: Tracks license renewal, cost survey, wage report (Sept. 1), SDAT report (April 15), MPRIME license upload and minimum wage changes.

forms.name: Client Record Release Authorization
forms.purpose: Written consent to release client information.

forms.name: Caregiver Rejection/Reassignment Record
forms.purpose: Documents a client's acceptance or rejection of a referred caregiver without retaliation.
